scope.description: Same four-node scenario as the executed revision (A/B bootstrapped, A snapshots, E added as a caught-up nonvoter, C added as a voter, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs so its configuration is the stale {A,B}, B partitioned, AddVoter E committing the two-server change {A,B,E} on A plus E, one client command applied on A), with one addition: while A still leads on the stale membership, the probe calls VerifyLeader on A and records the result, then observes whether the old majority {B,C} elects a leader in a higher term, and emits both together.
assumptions: VerifyLeader is the documented protection clients use to avoid returning stale data from a peer that has lost leadership.
The stale leader's confirmation uses the acknowledgements available to it under its in-memory configuration {A,B,E}, which is exactly the configuration its own log does not contain.
The old majority's election is decided independently of the stale leader because B is partitioned from A.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the configuration is current and the two-server change cannot arise.
Reads themselves are not issued; the observation is the confirmation call's result, not a data read.

basis.prefix: Identical to the executed revision: real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same stores, real client Apply, real transport partition and real healing; the only addition is a VerifyLeader call on the stale leader between the client write and the old side's election.

comparisons.description: An entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs must not be replaced after the partition heals.
After a client write returns success, every node following the same log must apply the same committed commands.
A node must not confirm leadership for a client while a different majority of the committed configuration has elected a leader in a higher term.

before.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter, commits four commands. A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds {A,B,C}; B is partitioned; A issues AddVoter E, which the stale base turns into the two-server change {A,B,E} and which commits on A plus E. The probe then issues one client command on A (committed with A and E) and finally heals the partition, observing the entry at the created index and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, so {A,B,E} commits with A and E alone once B is partitioned.
The client command is an ordinary Apply on the leader that has a quorum of the configuration recorded in its own log ({A,B,E}: A and E).
MockFSM records one entry per LogCommand applied, so its length is the number of committed commands that node's FSM has consumed.
Both sides keep running the protocol; the partition is applied by disconnecting in-memory transports in both directions.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create the disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration).
Leader concurrency is not asserted as a comparison here because its window depends on when the higher-term vote requests reach the stale leader.

revision_reason: This revision adds the client-contract observation to the same scenario: after the silent change and the acknowledged client write, the probe asks the stale-membership leader to confirm leadership (VerifyLeader) while it still leads with the promoted voter's acknowledgements, and then records whether the old majority elects a leader in a higher term in the same run. Predictions, earlier observations and comparisons are unchanged; one comparison is added for the new event.
